title: Canonical isomorphisms of individual finite affine Cech terms
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings with an $R$-algebra structure on $S$, let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be separated, let $U_i$ be a finite family of affine opens of $X$, and let $M$ be a quasi-coherent module, using [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $X_S$, $g:X_S\to X$, $f_S:X_S\to\operatorname{Spec}S$, $N=g^*M$ and its adjunction unit be those of [def-pc-base-change], [def-pc-flat-cohomology-comparison]. Put $V_i=g^{-1}U_i$. Let $P,Q$ be the module presheaves with scalars restricted along the structure maps from $R,S$ respectively; put $C=\check C(U,P)$, $A=S\otimes_R C$ degreewise, and $B=\check C(V,Q)$, using [pqf-def-cohomology], [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. For each tuple $y$ let $W_y=\bigcap_l U_{y_l}$ and $W'_y=\bigcap_l V_{y_l}$, and choose the inclusion $h_y:W'_y\subseteq g^{-1}W_y$ (it is automatic). Let $a_y,z_y$ be the product coordinates of $C,B$ restricted to these intersections. There exist $S$-module isomorphisms $e_k:A^k\cong B^k$ for all $k\geq0$ such that $z_y(e_k(b\otimes x))=b|_{W'_y}\cdot\eta_{M,W_y}(a_y(x))|_{W'_y}$ for every $b\in S$ and $x\in C^k$. This asserts no compatibility with differentials and does not require that the family covers $X$.

proof.text: For every nonempty tuple of affine opens, use the affine diagonal criterion for the separated morphism over Spec R and finite nonempty induction to prove the intersection affine. Inverse images commute with infima, so the corresponding intersection on X_S equals the inverse image of this affine open. Use the base-change projections defined in def-pc-flat-cohomology-comparison for this inverse-image calculation.
Apply the canonical affine scalar-extension section equivalence separately to each tuple, obtaining an S-linear equivalence and its pure-tensor formula.

Promote the existing Cech coordinate additive equivalence to a linear equivalence. Identify categorical scalar extension with S tensor_R C.X k, preserving pure tensors. Transport the source coordinate equivalence through TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.congr, apply TensorProduct.piRight for the finite tuple type, take LinearEquiv.piCongrRight of the affine section equivalences, and apply the inverse target coordinate equivalence. Convert the resulting linear equivalence to a ModuleCat isomorphism. Cancel the coordinate equivalence with its inverse and apply the affine pure-tensor formula to prove the required equation. This also covers empty index types since piRight and piCongrRight admit the empty family.
